title: EEG recordings during sham neurofeedback in virtual reality
description: This dataset contains 32-channel EEG recordings acquired during a sham neurofeedback experiment in a virtual reality environment. The study examined how feedback valence (positive, negative, or none) modulates alpha-band activity during an attentional task. Each participant completed positive, negative, control, and resting-state (eyes open/eyes closed) conditions.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 32-channel Compumedics NeuroScan SynAmps RT amplifier and Ag/AgCl passive electrodes on an elastic cap following the extended 10-20 system. Stimuli were delivered through a VR headset developed in Unity3D and synchronized with event markers. Each feedback condition consisted of four blocks of about 2 minutes, and the resting-state condition alternated eyes open and eyes closed (1.5 min each). Original .cnt files were converted to BIDS with MNE-BIDS.
